name: Guinness
hook: Dublin's 1759 brewery, its dark stout, and the record book it gave the world.

facts.label: Arthur Guinness
facts.statement: Arthur Guinness founded the brewery at St. James's Gate in Dublin in 1759; in 2009 the city marked the brewery's 250th anniversary.

facts.label: stout
facts.statement: Guinness is a stout — a dark, hoppy beer that has been the brewery's classic product for more than two centuries.

facts.label: Guinness World Records
facts.statement: The brewery's Guinness Book of Records became Guinness World Records, which is why "According to Guinness" introduces any superlative.

facts.label: record-book superlatives
facts.statement: Guinness calls the London Bridge the largest antique ever sold, a pumpkin the heaviest fruit or vegetable, and a chicken-sized dinosaur the smallest.

facts.label: the widget
facts.statement: The widget inside a can of Guinness, which produces its creamy head, won a Queen's Award for technological advancement in 1991.

facts.label: Christmas 1939
facts.statement: For Christmas 1939 Guinness sent a bottle to every member of the British forces stationed in France.
